questions.question:
**Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.**

Her evaluation will give / me a best indication of / where I stand in the class.

options.text: where I stand in the class.

questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **me a best indication of**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The use of "**a**" before "**best indication**" is incorrect.
 
• It should be "**the best indication**".
 
• The given sentence implies that there is a single, specific indication that is considered the best among all possibilities.
 
• "**A**" is used when we are referring to a non-specific item or thing. It introduces a noun that is not already known to the listener or is being mentioned for the first time.
 
• "**The**" is used when we are referring to a specific item, person, or group that is already known to both the speaker and the listener or that can be easily identified from the context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

**The correct sentence would be**: *"Her evaluation will give me the best indication of where I stand in the class."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: "Where I stand in the class" is grammatically correct.
 
• **Option 2**: "Her evaluation will give" is grammatically correct.

questions.question:
**Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.**

I stare out into the really __amazingly__ dark night.
questions.solution:

• **For example- ***Amazingly, the bullet did not penetrate his brain.*
 
 
 
• Marked option "**obviously**" implies that something is clear or evident. (स्पष्ट या प्रत्यक्षतः)
 
 
• **For example- ***She obviously feels that it was important enough to make a stand.*

• Hence "**obviously**" is a better fit than the other options.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• "**There**" is a location adverb and is not appropriate in this context.

• Option 3: "**Chosen there**" is incorrect because "chosen" is a past participle form of the verb "choose" and needs an auxiliary verb to complete the verb phrase (e.g. have chosen). "There" is still incorrect in this context.
